g.text: 1. Create a short URL from a long URL
2. Open a short URL → redirect to the original
- Unique codes (strong); new link live in ~1 s
- Click counts may lag a few minutes
- A created link is never lost
Account management · editing a link's destination · QR codes · analytics dashboards · full malware scanning
- Writes: 100M/month ≈ 40/s (~100/s peak) → one store handles it
- Reads: 1B/day ≈ 12K/s (~50K/s peak) → cache in front of the store
- Storage: 6B rows × 500 B ≈ 3 TB (≈ 9 TB replicated) → shard by key
- Cache: 10M hot links × 500 B ≈ 5 GB → one Redis node + replicas
- Code length: 62^6 ≈ 57B > 6B → 7 base62 chars gives headroom
- Storage is small (~9 TB); most cost is redirect servers + cache
- One region with replicas; multi-region only for a global latency target
- Alert on redirect p99, 5xx rate, cache hit rate, Kafka consumer lag
- Canary rollouts for the redirect service (it's on every click)
- Store TTL can lag days → redirect also checks expires_at
- Abuse: rate limits, blocklist on create, async scan of new links
First to break: the Redis shard holding a viral link
→ the in-process cache on redirect servers absorbs it
short_code · custom aliases share the table
